title: What Was It Before It Broke? Pick One 🔨
description:
What was it before it broke: a key, a bulb or a vase? Pick one before the shards fly back together, then check the last seconds.

We drew one object, cracked it into about 56 shards around the point where the hammer lands, and simulated every shard as a rigid piece: gravity, spin, friction, bounces off the floor and walls, and collisions between shards. The rebuild is that recording played backward, so the shards lift, fly back and lock together, outer pieces first, and it speeds up as it goes. The whole object appears only in the last 1.5 seconds. Then the hammer strikes and the same recording plays forward, so the video loops exactly. Slow-motion gravity: a toy recording, not real glass physics.
Shapes, picture and sound are generated by code (seed 442), with no footage, samples or stock media.
Got it right? +1 streak. Which one did you pick?
#simulation #satisfying #shatter
pinned_comment: Key, bulb or vase: what was it before it broke? Pick before the shards lock together. The rebuild is the shatter recording played backward.
synthetic_media_disclosure_reason: Clearly stylized 2D animation of an abstract object breaking; a toy physics recording that could not be mistaken for real footage, people, places or events.
